Ecolution

Ecolution will be remembered as one of the first companies to produce high quality hemp clothing. They helped create the demand that is fueling the current expansion of the hemp industry. Along with other stalwarts including The Ohio Hempery and Headcase, Ecolution has attended Eco Expos, Fashion Boutique Shows, Hemp Trade Shows, and yes, the Hemp Expo at the Cannabis Cup. Their unabashed devotion to all aspects of cannabis resulted in some "hemp only" companies & organizations to treat them more like pariahs than pioneers. Their disgust with the drug war should be commended, not condemned.

To Steve, Eric, Etienne, Rachel, and all the rest:

THANKS FOR EVERYTHING, KEEP UP THE FIGHT AND ALL THE BAST!! -- John Dvorak)

Ecolution is closing its doors

Ecolution <webmstr@ecolution.com>

An Open Letter to the Hemp Community from Steve DeAngelo:

I am writing to notify my associates, colleagues, and friends in the hemp community that Ecolution will be closing its doors.

Ecolution was founded in 1992 on a very limited amount of capital by a group of human rights activists and music industry veterans. We dedicated ourselves to producing new and innovative hemp products, while using only ethical and sustainable production methods and raw materials. We decided to get into the hemp business because of our love for the plant.

Within a few years, we achieved many technical breakthroughs: producing the first textile grade hemp yarn in Eastern Europe, the world’s first 100% hemp denim, the world’s first hemp plaid and striped textiles, the world’s first 100% hemp knits, and the world’s first 100% hemp writing paper. Ecolution was also notable for what it did not do: we did not adulterate our hemp with cotton, purchase it from China, or tone down our advocacy of the full legalization of all forms of cannabis.

Our strategy was to produce a garment of the highest quality in the most ethical way possible. This strategy met with great public support. We quickly developed customers in all 50 states and 22 foreign countries. Our sales tripled every year, reaching $1.65 million in 1997. We were recognized throughout the industry for dedication to product quality and exemplary integrity. However, the strategy also had great costs. Our ethical positions on China and cotton left us with narrow margins. Some in the industry shunned us due to our outspoken views on legalization. Initial research and development investments required huge sums of money, leaving us with no reserve funds for operating contingencies.

By 1998, the company was in a critical situation. A massive outpouring of public support had catapulted us to the forefront of the hemp garment trade. Growth was phenomenal, but financial resources were insufficient to cover the expenses associated with it. Unpaid bills climbed to a dangerous level. At the same time, the hemp industry matured. Many new manufacturers entered the market, building on our early research and development efforts. Some of these companies were started by seasoned garment industry professionals with years of experience. By blending cotton with their hemp or by purchasing inexpensively sewn Chinese garments, they beat our prices. Consumers having difficulties accepting the high price of hemp were attracted to these products. Our sales flattened, increasing our financial stress.

The difficulties which Ecolution faced were exacerbated by the time and experiential limitations of its founders. Our backgrounds were human rights activism and rock music, not manufacturing and export/import. We put ethical concerns before profits and had to accept lower margins than the company could sustain. In addition to overcoming the additional burdens presented by this rather novel decision making approach, we also had to teach ourselves every aspect of a very complex business. We made some mistakes along the way. As the hemp industry matured and competition became more intense, these handicaps became ever more debilitating. The incredible support we received from the buying public was sufficient to sustain us in the early years of the industry, but it could not protect us forever from the forces of the market.

At the beginning of this year we were faced with a harsh reality. Consumers were consistently choosing the products of our lower priced competitors. The overwhelming consumer support of our early days had severely eroded. If we did not find a way to reduce the cost of our products, we would not survive. Unfortunately, the only sufficient means of lowering our costs would be to renounce our long standing positions regarding cotton and China. As hempsters, and as human rights activists, we could not bring ourselves to compromise our ethics in the name of profit. We would rather shut our doors than put poison in hemp, or to produce it with slave labor.

After much internal discussion and soul searching, we have made the difficult decision to retire from the field of play. Unless a buyer can be found quickly, Ecolution will close its doors on May 18, 1999. We are looking for an experienced marketer who might want to carry on the Ecolution message and business. Anyone with talent, motivation and a modest investment should contact us quickly.

Last chance Sale: Until May 18 we are holding an across the board sale. Any order of over $250 will receive a 5% discount. Any order over $500 will receive a 10% discount and any order over $1000 will receive a 15% discount. (Sorry, this is cash only.) We still have a wide assortment of our clothing, Adidas shoes, twine, hats and accessories. (certain sizes or colors may be in short supply.) If you are interested, ask our salespeople about special prices on closeout merchandise.

Any unsold merchandise as well as the other assets of the corporation will be sold at a public auction on May 22, 1998 at our location. If you would like details of the auction please call or see: http://www.ecolution.com/auction.html All remaining corporate assets will be sold at this auction including our modern 8 station computer system, phone system, fax machine, software, copy machine, warehouse equip, office furniture, the corporate name and trademarks and a wide variety of trade show fixtures. Details are available on our website.

If all goes well, Ecolution, Inc. will be able to wrap up its affairs with all of its accounts paid. If Ecolution currently owes you money, you will receive a mailed version of this letter including a proof of claim form. Please complete this form and return it to our office before September 1, 1999. We have enlisted the help of N.T. Arrington, a licensed and bonded business liquidator.

I would like to thank all of you who have been so very generous in your support of the Ecolution vision-our investors, employees, customers, suppliers, and colleagues in the hemp industry. You are far too numerous to list by individual name, but you all know who you are. It is our sincere hope that we have carried the faith and the trust you placed in us in a good way. From the bottom of our hearts, we thank you. May the Great Spirit guide you and protect you, and one day set us all free.

Steve DeAngelo plans to continue to articulate and defend the values embodied by Ecolution; to stay involved with the hemp industry; to write screenplays, books and articles about cannabis; and of course to fight for freedom everywhere. Please stay in touch with him at the following:

Steve DeAngelo
